name: Kettlebell Body — Complete Sales Process
note: Reconstructed from a two-column PDF process map. Phase numbering follows the document; phases 7-10 (presentation and close) are referenced by the map but not enumerated on the supplied pages, so scoring covers phases 1-6, the five objection plays, and phase 11.

checks.text: Read back setter notes / application so they feel seen
Set the four-part frame: where you are, where you want to go, what's in the way, what you need
Get frame agreement — 'Does that work?'
Open question: 'What are you potentially looking for help with?'
Age, height, current weight
Work — and whether it's desk-bound or on their feet
Health conditions, own or hereditary
Injuries, chronic pain, movement limitations — and how long
Typical training week and actual days trained
Results seen from current training
Current diet / whether following anything
Sleep — quantity and quality
Energy through the day

phases.name: Goals — Surface to Deep
phases.intent: Move from what to WHY. This is where the real buying decision is made.

checks.text: Aesthetics & function: what would you change, one thing
Mobility, strength, energy — or something else
Something physical you want to do but can't right now
Bridge: 'Outside of the physical, what's actually driving this right now?'
'When you're moving better, what does that actually do for you?'
'Who else does that impact?'
Drive through to kids, marriage, legacy, identity or longevity
Reflect back: 'So this isn't really about the weight — it's about X. Is that right?'
What have you tried before?
What happened with that?
Why do you feel it didn't stick?
What's the one thing actually getting in the way?
Let them name the gap: no structure, no progression, no accountability, wrong knowledge, inconsistency
'The information isn't the problem. Why can't you stick to it on your own?'

phases.name: Consequence Frame
phases.intent: Make the cost of inaction real.

checks.text: 'If nothing changes — what does life look like over the next two years?'
'Is that something you're willing to settle for?'
'Why not?'
'Are you ready to draw a line in the sand on this?'

phases.name: Commitment Check
phases.intent: Get a genuine verbal yes BEFORE presenting anything.

checks.text: 'Do you believe you can actually get there with the right structure and the right person in your corner?'
'If you had everything you needed — is there any reason you wouldn't go all in on this?'
Only move forward once you have a clear YES; if hesitation surfaces, return to Phase 5

phases.name: Payment & Onboarding
phases.intent: Complete every step before you hang up.

checks.text: Step 1 — Collect payment
Step 2 — Schedule the onboarding call with Trevor
Step 3 — Confirm the agreement email arrived and have them sign it ON the call
Step 4 — Tell them to read the welcome email, click the Skool link to join the community, and complete the onboarding questionnaire before the Trevor call

objection_plays.trigger: I need to think about it
key_moves: Do you feel what we've gone through CAN get you to [goal]?
What makes you feel it can?
So what's actually coming up that's preventing you from getting started?
Thinking isn't the problem. Deciding is.
The way you've been approaching this brought you here — when do you make a different decision?
That man you want to be — how does HE decide right now?
Are you sure? Nothing else keeping you from being 100% in?

objection_plays.trigger: I need to talk to my wife
key_moves: Money aside — do you personally feel this CAN get you to [goal]?
When you talk to her, what obstacles might come up?
Is there any reason she would NOT want you stronger and less in pain?
Is this genuinely needing her input — or asking permission to bet on yourself?
This isn't a joint decision like buying a house. Is that responsibility hers or yours?
If stuck: put down a deposit, go talk to her, full refund if she says no

objection_plays.name: Money — Open Wallet
key_moves: ISOLATE FIRST: 'Finances aside — nothing else keeping you from 100%?'
'You're not in a SHOULD I place, you're in a HOW place'
'Most clients pay upfront, but for some we break it up. Want to explore making it work?'
'Are you comfortable having an open, honest conversation about exactly where you're at financially?'
FINANCIAL PICTURE: cash on hand
FINANCIAL PICTURE: what's left over each month after bills
FINANCIAL PICTURE: how many credit cards
FINANCIAL PICTURE: available credit total per card
FINANCIAL PICTURE: used vs available
FINANCIAL PICTURE: crypto, stocks, investments
Are you ever going to have another Thanksgiving? Another busy season?
Things never slow down. When does it actually become the right time?
The longer you wait the harder this gets — metabolism slows, injuries compound
What if all you had to do was show up and everything else was handled?
The only thing you can control is right now
So what's actually coming up that's preventing you from getting started?
Would it be fair to say you're looking for certainty?
Do we run toward pleasure or away from pain — which is driving you?
BRIDGE: I'm not asking you to see the whole other side, just take the first step
PLANE: fear of the flight doesn't mean you never reach the destination
BURNED BEFORE: if you got hurt in a relationship once, do you never trust again?
But how will you know if you never actually try?

known_gaps_in_script.gap: No play for a clinical / medical-fit objection
known_gaps_in_script.detail: When a prospect's physio or surgeon rules out the core kettlebell movement library, there is no scripted path. The rep is left improvising a partial-value reframe. Seen in the Tyron Giuliani call.

known_gaps_in_script.gap: No play for 'a cheaper alternative already worked for me'
known_gaps_in_script.detail: Objection C assumes the blocker is capacity to pay, not perceived value against a functioning low-cost substitute. Seen in the Badrane Hriouch call, where the anchor was a $29/mo coach.
